This anonymous roof is the workplace of an inferred carpenter's household (5 of 11 this layer infers): hh_inf_carpenter_north_05 in data/residents/households/. THE ROOF'S OWN EXISTENCE, POSITION AND FOOTPRINT REMAIN CONJECTURAL and are unchanged by the adoption; what the adoption adds is an argued occupant instead of an anonymous count-unit. The occupant is hypothesised from the town's demonstrable needs - the 1835 census of 3,265 people in 398 dwellings against the trades Andreas's 1833 roster names - and is not a person: no name is claimed and no figure is drawn.

persons.name: Henry Cobb
persons.note: HYPOTHESISED, AND NOT A PERSON. No source names this resident and none is claimed to: the record asserts that a town of 3,265 people in 398 dwellings held at least this many households of this trade, and asserts nothing whatever about any individual. THE NAME IS INVENTED TOO, and `name_basis` beside it says so and says which pool it came from: this record used to carry a bare designation instead, on the reasoning that a surname would make it look like the documented layer, but a town of designations does not read as a town and the grade, this note and name_basis all say plainly which layer this is. No figure is drawn (docs/LIBERTIES.md L1). THE FIFTH OF 11 CARPENTER HOUSEHOLDS THIS LAYER INFERS. THE TRADE THE TOWN NEEDED MOST AND THE ONE THE DOCUMENTED LAYER UNDER-COUNTS WORST. The 1835 town census counts 3,265 people in 398 dwellings; Andreas's roster of the fall of 1833 describes a settlement of a few dozen buildings, and the reconstruction specification puts 665 roofs on the ground by July 1835. Several hundred of those roofs went up inside eighteen months. Even at a crew of three raising a one-room frame cottage in three weeks, that is on the order of forty carpenter-years of work in a year and a half. Andreas names four carpenters and one ship carpenter in the whole of the 1833 town. Ten carpenter households are inferred against the schedule's eight W2 carpenter-or-joiner shops, because a house carpenter worked on the frame in the street and not in a shop: the shop count is a floor under the trade, not a measure of it. ONE FURTHER CARPENTER HOUSEHOLD, 2026-08-14, AND THE ROOF IS THE REASON RATHER THAN A NEW FINDING ABOUT THE TRADE. The count above is stated as a floor in its own last clause, and what held it at ten was method rule 5: every household must be housed, and housing one where no anonymous roof of the right family and district stands means raising an invented building. The block parcel at Randolph and Wells has since put a D3 one-room frame cottage on the plat in the South Division - a roof the 665-roof programme had already counted, in the family this layer houses nine of its ten carpenters in. Adopting it raises no building, invents no position and moves no other record; it puts an argued occupant under a roof that was standing anonymously. Eleven carpenter households are inferred, still against eight W2 shops and still a floor.

METHOD: the count comes from the occupation census in data/reconstruction/1835_inferred_household_programme.json, which calibrates every trade against three things this project already holds - the 1835 town census (3,265 people, 398 dwellings), Andreas's roster of the fall of 1833 (about fifty named people, most with a trade, in a settlement of some 350), and the reconstruction specification's roof schedule, whose workshop and store family targets are treated as the ceiling on a trade rather than as its measure. Every count is stated NET of the documented layer: this dataset infers a tradesman only where it cannot name one.
